runs.content: Saturday's rotation is a full sweep — skim every domain's overview/index page instead of deep-reading one, biasing toward cross-domain connections over investigation ideas. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-18, Thursday), the wiki was quiet: log.md shows exactly one new item — a podcast-summarizer run today created podcasts/podcast-dividend-talk-art-of-the-turnaround.md, a retrospective episode built entirely around 'what separates a genuine turnaround from a value trap' and position sizing when a dividend payer is under stress. That single new page produced one connection and no new investigation ideas (nothing else changed this week to surface anything new). Cross-domain connection: the episode's turnaround-vs-value-trap framework lands directly on finance/investor-letters/source-burry-build-a-bear-part1-2026-08-29.md — Burry's live, unresolved Build-A-Bear (BBW) long, which shows exactly the diagnostic signals the episode teaches in the abstract (no kitchen-sink impairment/write-down despite the earnings miss, a new CEO reversing the specific 'plushy push' brand-dilution mistake that caused the stumble, growth capex raised not cut) while Burry himself is explicitly 'no rush to add; awaiting the 10-Q' before Part 2's valuation verdict. BBW isn't a dividend payer, so this sharpens rather than directly extends the episode's own dividend-growth frame, but neither page cross-links the other despite describing the same judgment call. Concrete next step: once Fred listens, add a line to the Burry source page's See Also citing the episode's framework as a lens for the pending Part 2 verdict. Thursday's rotation focus is Books + Podcasts. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-15, Tuesday), a scheduler outage blocked most scheduled tasks on 09-16 and 09-17 (see memory/mcp_local_servers_connect_timeout_2026_09_15) — the only genuinely new material this week was the 2026-09-15 book-recommender's September batch in books/suggestions.md; Podcasts had no new pages or recommendations at all. Both findings today trace back to that single new batch. Investigation idea: the batch recommends Sorkin's '1929' explicitly because it 'lands squarely on his live AI-capex-bubble tracking (Djukanovic, Klement, Grantham)' — but checking those pages shows the fit is thinner than the recommendation implies: ai-tech/source-ai-supremacy-compute-demand-disrupt-america-2026-08-10.md cites 1929 as only one number in a margin-debt checklist, and finance/investor-letters/source-djukanovic-ai-capital-cycle-2026-06-26.md reaches for the 1873 Panic of the railroads, not 1929, as its historical anchor — none of the wiki's AI-bubble pages actually work through 1929's own credit/margin-call mechanics the way Sorkin's Fed-minutes-sourced book would. Cross-domain connection: the same batch's 'Rise of the Machines' (drone warfare, Ukraine) recommendation independently names both finance/ideas/idea-rheinmetall.md and technology/source-guardian-fire-point-ukraine-missiles-2026-07-27.md in its own 'Why Fred' text — the identical unlinked pair a 2026-08-01 thinker entry already flagged as open. That the book-recommender's own reasoning (built from reading history, not from reading either page) independently rediscovers the same gap from a different domain and a different automated process is a second, distinct signal it's real. Neither book is ingested yet (recommendations only) — both concrete next steps start with adding them to reading-list.md's aspirational section.
